summary: President Trump has signed a new national space policy aimed at enabling 1,000 U.S. rocket launches per year, highlighting major momentum in the launch sector as SpaceX reached its 100th Falcon launch of the year and completed a static-fire test of Starship ahead of the vehicle's first orbital flight. In civil spaceflight news, NASA's Artemis II crew is set to receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor while the agency considers updates to astronaut training for future commercial space stations. Military space developments include U.S. Space Command relocating 200 personnel to Alabama this year as leadership prepares for future threats to ground segments and cislunar operations; elsewhere in defense, eight people were killed in a contractor plane crash near a remote Alaska radar site, and Taiwan proposed a record $35 billion defense budget. Commercial sector highlights feature a new Novaspace forecast projecting more than 6,500 Earth observation satellites will launch by 2035, SpaceWERX announcing its 2026 STRATFI awardees, and hybrid engine developer Letara raising ¥2.6 billion. Scientific discoveries include NASA's Curiosity rover finding a massive field of polygons on Mars, interplanetary spacecraft capturing previously hidden coronal mass ejection components, and researchers gathering initial experimental evidence that strong magnetic fields can suppress stellar eruptions. Internationally, China announced plans for a lunar mission to locate water ice. Readers should watch for Japan's upcoming Mars moon sample-return mission following the recent unveiling of its spacecraft ahead of a scheduled Oct. 19 launch.
